emerging_technology: Data-center AI GPU accelerators for generative-AI inference
intended_application: Cloud-based training and inference for rapidly changing computer-vision and multimodal models used to inspect commercial building images
business_need: Run short, bursty model experiments and launch customer pilots quickly without committing scarce capital to a data center
users_stakeholders: ML engineers, product managers, startup customers, cloud operations, founders, and investors
adoption_posture: Aggressive leading-edge adopter that accepts controlled technical risk in exchange for iteration speed
capabilities_constraints: Strong PyTorch and container skills; no data-center staff; variable and uncertain demand; limited capital; models can run in approved U.S. cloud regions; engineering can port selected workloads but cannot maintain multiple production stacks indefinitely
risk_consequence_context: Missed product milestones and runaway cloud spend are material; failures are reversible through rollback; no clinical or safety-critical use; customer images still require contractual security controls
management_question: Which accelerator access strategy should the startup test over the next six months to maximize iteration speed while preserving credible options beyond a single GPU vendor?
time_horizon: Immediate experiments and customer pilots over six months; architecture reassessment every quarter
additional_context: Assessment date: 2026-11-13. Keep the emerging technology constant while changing application, organization, adoption posture, capabilities, consequences, and ownership model.
